record.original_question: Let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B^n, R^m) satisfy the degenerate elliptic system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · |∇u|^{n-2}∇u, where Ω is an antisymmetric matrix-valued field in L^n(R^{m x m} ⊗ R^n). Does this antisymmetric-potential structure force u to be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5. Let u ∈ W1,n(Bn, Rm) satisfy a system of the form (2.6) - div (|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · |∇u|^{n-2}∇u.
Assume that Ω = (Ω^α_ij) ∈ L^n(R^{m×m} ⊗ R^n) is antisymmetric, i.e. Ω^α_ij = -Ω^α_ji for all 1 ≤ i, j ≤ m. Is it true that u is continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$, $m\ge 1$, and let $B^n\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ denote the open unit ball. Suppose $u\in W^{1,n}(B^n,\mathbb{R}^m)$ is a weak solution of the degenerate elliptic system
$$-\operatorname{div}\! igl(|
abla u|^{n-2}
abla u igr)\;=\;\Omega\cdot |
abla u|^{n-2}
abla u\qquad	ext{in } B^n,$$
where $\Omega=(\Omega^{\alpha}_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le m,\,1\le\alpha\le n}\in L^{n}(B^n,\mathfrak{so}(m)\otimes\mathbb{R}^n)$ is antisymmetric in the matrix indices, i.e.\ $\Omega^{\alpha}_{ij}=-\Omega^{\alpha}_{ji}$ for all $1\le i,j\le m$ and all $1\le \alpha\le n$. The right-hand side is interpreted componentwise as $(\Omega\cdot |
abla u|^{n-2}
abla u)^i = \sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{\alpha=1}^n \Omega^{\alpha}_{ij}\,|
abla u|^{n-2}\partial_\alpha u^j$.

Question: Does the antisymmetry of $\Omega$ alone (with $\Omega\in L^n$) force every such weak solution $u$ to be continuous in $B^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work establishes continuity of W^{1,n} solutions to n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potentials only under stronger Lorentz-space assumptions (e.g. $\Omega\in L^{n,2}$ or gradient in $L^{n,2}$), via Coulomb gauges and conservation-law techniques (Rivière; Hörter–Lamm–Schikorra, Math. Ann. 2024). The case of a bare $L^n$ antisymmetric potential, which is the natural analogue of Rivière's $n=2$ continuity theorem in higher dimensions, does not appear to be resolved in the literature, and the problem is still posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Regularizing properties of n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potentials in Lorentz spaces
status_evidence.snippet: n-harmonic maps into manifolds are continuous if their gradient belongs to the Lorentz-space L^(n,2) — a trivial and optimal assumption if n=2.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art continuity results require a Lorentz refinement beyond L^n, suggesting the pure-L^n case is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Conservation Laws for p-Harmonic Systems with Antisymmetric Potentials and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Extends Rivière's conservation-law approach to p-harmonic systems with antisymmetric potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity continues to develop the framework, indicating that full continuity under L^n alone remains an active question.
